domain_title: Data, privacy, confidentiality and intellectual property
title: Invisible or untraceable data flows
canonical_definition: Data origin, ownership, transformation, transmission, retention or reuse cannot be reliably established.

conditions: All AI systems that receive, generate, retrieve or learn from data.
Record the assessed release, operating scope and evidence that supports any applicability decision.

primary_questions.question: Does the case exhibit Invisible or untraceable data flows: Data origin, ownership, transformation, transmission, retention or reuse cannot be reliably established.
Do implemented workflows, data paths or operations show unknown prompt sources, undocumented provider fields, or outputs reused without provenance?
Does current evidence test presence or scoped absence of Invisible or untraceable data flows, or does it remain unknown?

conditions: Refer verified invisible or untraceable data flows to the accountable authority before progression where the condition materially affects the requested operating scope.

normative_source_mappings.relevant_locator: NIST AI 100-1, MAP 2.3 (PDF p. 32), MAP 4.1 (PDF p. 32), MEASURE 2.1 (PDF p. 34)
normative_source_mappings.mapping_rationale: The voluntary framework provides guidance on documenting data suitability, third-party component risks and evaluation data. The SAE criteria define the object-specific rules. Confirm any binding obligation through the accountable authority and its applicable source.

failure_mechanism: The declared or implemented control can be unreliable where the source, permission or owner of material input is unknown in the controlling records. The mechanism can have an operational effect where an actual prompt or derived output contains data from an unrecorded destination or cannot be traced through a material transformation.
potential_consequences: An affected decision may be impossible to trace or correct when an input is invalidated.

atomic_tests.test: Compare the effective governance and design records. Determine whether the source, permission or owner of material input is unknown in the controlling records. Identify the system scope and the record that supports each conclusion.

Trace actual configurations or activity for the assessed release. Determine whether an actual prompt or derived output contains data from an unrecorded destination or cannot be traced through a material transformation. Attribute each observation to the specific path, time and decision.

Independently review representative lineage traces across normal, fallback, external and derived-data paths. Record whether each material mechanism was tested, the observed result and the scope limitations.

required_evidence.title: Effective design and governance records
required_evidence.description: Review the versioned owner decision and relevant specifications for evidence of whether the source, permission or owner of material input is unknown in the controlling records. Preserve material conflict and applicability context.

required_evidence.title: Observed condition or enforcement trace
required_evidence.description: Use effective configuration or dated operational records to determine whether an actual prompt or derived output contains data from an unrecorded destination or cannot be traced through a material transformation. Identify the version, affected paths and period represented.

required_evidence.title: Executed scoped comparison
required_evidence.description: Provide representative lineage traces across normal, fallback, external and derived-data paths. Include current scope, expected results, observed results, retained evidence and unresolved cases.

required_evidence.title: Independent review and limitations
required_evidence.description: An independent reviewer confirms the assessed version, completeness of coverage, result, limitations and whether a material change requires a new test.

required_artifacts: Representative lineage traces across normal, fallback, external and derived-data paths.
Current version and scope with all material failure paths and cases identified.
Expected and observed results, attributable records, and independent review of coverage and residual limitations.

sufficiency: Presence requires affirmative evidence for a material mechanism. Examine whether the source, permission or owner of material input is unknown in the controlling records, and separately check whether an actual prompt or derived output contains data from an unrecorded destination or cannot be traced through a material transformation. A supported mechanism may establish presence within its evidenced scope.
Keep unresolved or contradictory mechanisms UNKNOWN and preserve the competing records. Refer material interpretation conflicts to the accountable human authority.

Use TESTED_ABSENT only after a current, executed, successful and independently verified evaluation covers all material paths within scope. Use representative lineage traces across normal, fallback, external and derived-data paths. Reassess when material changes affect that scope.
evidence_rules.evidence_ceiling: A document can identify a declared gap. Effective configuration can demonstrate a reachable condition. Observed records support only their covered period and workflow. TESTED_ABSENT requires the complete scoped absence contract.
false_positive_guards: An alias or abstraction is compatible with traceability when it resolves to a versioned authoritative identifier.
Confirm that the observed or alleged condition applies to the current assessed release and a reachable path.
prohibited_inferences: A gap or UNKNOWN in B1 alone cannot establish AP-B1 presence.
Missing complaints, incident silence and unsuccessful collection cannot establish absence.
Model output and tactic selection grant no authority to approve, close a finding or accept risk.

finding_definitions.title: Design or intent shows invisible or untraceable data flows
Implementation or operating evidence shows invisible or untraceable data flows
Presence or tested absence of invisible or untraceable data flows is unresolved within scope
